description:
Decided in defk-dtw.14. A kernel local of type bitstring (signature name: bitstring) that starts as <<>> and is only appended to: acc = <<acc::bitstring, seg, ...>> with integer segments v::size(n) or v::k (unsigned, big-endian/MSB-first as Elixir's default). Also bit_size/1. It may be returned alone or in a tuple. Not supported: reading/indexing, float or binary segments, starting from an input bitstring, passing to another kernel (each compile error names the construct and hints at the limit).
Semantics: a segment value that doesn't fit n bits raises (a limit, same as array writes; Elixir truncates); n outside 0..64 raises (a limit). Elixir mode applies the same checks.
Runtime: a growable native buffer (doubling), kept in the frame across yields, freed on kernel exception and on process death. The NIF returns bytes + bit length; the generated Elixir wrapper makes the bitstring with <<b::bitstring-size(len), _::bitstring>> = bin.
Done when: tests in both modes cover the fit/width limits, empty output, non-byte-aligned output, an output that grows across forced yields (__defk_force_yields__/1), and cleanup on process kill mid-build; docs/language.md documents the construct and its limits; a Gorilla value-encoder kernel written with it gives bit-identical output to gorilla_stream's Elixir encoder.
title: Add the bitstring accumulator
